name: async: submit, hand back, resume when the work has landed
description: Validates the execution contract end to end rather than inferring it from an answer. Turn one submits a job and is told not to wait, so the turn ends with work pending; the `work_settled` event then proves the harness observed pending work and advanced it, the way the shell's watcher (src/invocations.ts) does between turns in production. Turn two resumes and must verify the landed output. The job is a URL upload, chosen because a local tool run finishes in about six seconds -- Galaxy's dispatch floor, not the data -- which is shorter than the model takes to write its reply, so a local tool cannot leave work pending at turn end. A remote fetch takes tens of seconds and needs no instance configuration, unlike the sleep tools that ship with Galaxy's functional tests.
inputs: Import this dataset into my history: https://zenodo.org/records/6803028/files/olympics.tsv?download=1 — submit it now and immediately tell me you have submitted it. Do not wait for it and do not check its state in this turn.
Is it finished? Tell me how many rows it has and confirm it landed successfully.
